title: Sales Enablement Playbook: Positioning, Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Daniel Kim
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's recommended positioning, messaging frameworks, competitive briefs, pitch deck outline, pricing guidance, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Intended audience: AEs, SDRs, solutions engineers, and field marketing. Use this document as the canonical source when preparing deal materials, enterprise RFP responses, and prospect briefings.

TL;DR (elevator pitch):
- Problem: Serving production LLMs reliably and economically is hard — teams face unpredictable latency, high per-token cost, and brittle operational tooling.
- Redwood solution: A unified inference platform with hosted, dedicated, and private deployments that makes inference predictable, cost-efficient, and observable.
- Core outcomes: predictable latency (p95 < configured SLO), lower unit cost via batching/caching and quantization guidance, and enterprise-ready security/compliance for regulated workloads.

Target personas and primary use cases:
- ML engineers / infra leads: performance, tooling, and model compatibility.
- Product engineers: response quality, structured outputs, and cost per feature.
- Platform/infra teams: SLA & isolation, private deployments, and auditability.
- Security/IT: data residency, KMS/HSM, SOC2/compliance evidence.

Messaging framework (Problem — Why now — Redwood value — Proof — CTA):
1) Problem: Cost and latency variance at scale.
   - Why now: Open model ecosystem & multi-vendor hardware increases variance and operational burden.
   - Redwood value: Unified runtime + smart routing + caching to stabilize unit economics and SLOs.
   - Proof: Verified model performance profiles, benchmark deck, reference customers (see Case Studies).
   - CTA: Run a 2-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated or Hosted with our benchmark harness.

2) Problem: Regulated workloads require private control plane and auditability.
   - Why now: More customers need on-prem/VPC and strict KMS controls.
   - Redwood value: Private deployment + audit logs + enterprise integrations (Okta, KMS).
   - Proof: SOC2 + customer private deployments (FinServe case study).
   - CTA: Request white-glove onboarding and security pack.

Competitive brief (at-a-glance):
| Differentiator | Redwood Inference | OpenCloudAI (large cloud) | ManagedLLM (API-first competitor) | SelfHostServe (open-source runtimes) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deployment modes | Hosted, Dedicated, Private (VPC & on-prem) | Hosted, Managed K8s | Hosted only | Self-hosted runtime only |
| Predictable throughput | Yes — reserved GPU pools + autoscale | Limited — noisy neighbor risk | Best-effort | Depends on customer ops |
| Cost controls | Batching, KV caching, quantization guidance | Limited visibility on kernel selection | Pricing opaque, limited batching controls | Manual tuning required |
| Observability & tooling | Token-level cost, model-level dashboards, rollouts, tracing | Basic metrics, vendor lock-in | Minimal observability | Varies by community tools |
| Enterprise security | Private control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SOC2 | Strong cloud security but limited private deployment options | Enterprise features add cost | Depends on implementation |
| Best fit | Rapid production adoption + enterprise SLOs and security | Customers already on one public cloud | Simpler experimentation & prototyping | Teams with mature ops and time to manage |

Key objection-handling scripts:
- “Your pricing is higher than public API”: 
  - Response: Compare unit economics — after batching, caching and reserved capacity customers typically see 20–50% lower per-token costs vs run-it-yourself or multiple small API calls. Offer to run an ROI calc with customer workload.
- “We can self-host open-source models cheaper”:
  - Response: Self-hosting transfers hidden ops and reliability costs. Redwood's unified runtime reduces time-to-production and lowers ongoing ops overhead; we can show case studies and SLO comparisons.
- “We need on-prem / air-gapped”:
  - Response: Redwood Private supports on-prem packaging + control plane options and integrates with customer KMS/HSM. Provide our onprem packaging checklist and refer to the private-deployments repo.

Pitch deck recommended outline (slide-by-slide):
1) Title + Ask (1 slide): Quick one-line value prop and the commercial ask (pilot, PO, capacity commit).
2) Customer pain + why now (1 slide): latency, cost, resiliency bullet points specific to the prospect.
3) Redwood platform overview (1 slide): Hosted/Dedicated/Private modes + routing/caching/runtime optimizations.
4) How it works (1–2 slides): Smart routing, batching, KV caching, model catalog + kernel selection. Include a simple diagram.
5) Performance evidence (2 slides): p95 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens for common model sizes. Use Redwood-verified benchmarks.
6) Operational guarantees & SLAs (1 slide): Sample SLOs (e.g., p95 latency 200–400 ms for common configs, 99.95% uptime for Dedicated, 24/7 support SLAs).
7) Security & compliance (1 slide): Data residency, SOC2, KMS, network isolation, audit logs.
8) Pricing & packaging (1 slide): Example tiers and negotiation levers (see Pricing Guidance).
9) Case studies & references (1–2 slides): 2 short wins with metrics.
10) Implementation plan (1 slide): Kickoff, pilot scope, success criteria, timeline (4–8 weeks typical for pilot to production).
11) Ask & next steps (1 slide): Technical workshop, security review, PO/commit.

Assets to include with deck:
- One-pager ROI calculator (spreadsheet).
- Technical deep-dive PDF for SRE/Platform teams.
- Security pack: SOC2 summary, pen test summary, network diagrams, onprem packaging checklist.
- Demo script and test dataset for native benchmark.

Pricing guidance (rules of thumb and negotiation levers):
- Pricing components: base platform fee (for enterprise/private), usage charge (per-token or per-embedding unit), reserved capacity discount (committed monthly/annual), professional services/implementation, premium support/observability retention add-ons.
- Example starter buckets (for prospect conversations):
  - Self-serve/Hosted: pay-as-you-go per 1k tokens + token rate table in appendix.
  - Dedicated: commit to N GPUs/month — discounted per-token equivalent and guaranteed latency window.
  - Private: platform/license + deployment fee + optional ongoing support.
- Negotiation levers: commit term length, committed capacity, usage smoothing guarantees, exclusivity on capacity during peak windows, bumped SLA (price uplift), implementation fee credits.
- Example discounting matrix (guidance):
  - Small pilot (< $10k ARR): minimal discount; include free onboarding hours.
  - Mid (10k–50k ARR): 10–20% off list on committed capacity + 30–60 days free onboarding.
  - Enterprise (> 50k ARR): 20–40%+ depending on multi-year commitment and add-ons (private deployments costly up-front).

Case studies (short, anonymized customer stories):
1) Acme Retail — personalized search and recommendation
- Background: Mid-market e-commerce chain using retrieval-augmented generation for product discovery.
- Solution: Migrated generation & reranking pipelines to Redwood Dedicated; enabled KV caching for session-level reuse.
- Outcome: 3x throughput, p95 generation latency reduced from 850ms to 280ms, and estimated 37% lower inference cost after batching and quantization profile changes.
- Contactable reference: yes (SE-approved).

2) FinServe (financial services) — secure private deployment for customer Q&A
- Background: Regulated fintech needing on-prem inference for PII-sensitive documents.
- Solution: Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS, isolated control plane, and audit log configuration.
- Outcome: Successful SOC2 audit integration, pilot → production in 10 weeks, reduced compliance review time by 60% vs internal build.

Security FAQ (for prospect briefings):
Q: Where does customer data live?
A: Hosted: selectable region replicas and configurable retention policies. Dedicated: tenant isolation in reserved pools. Private: customer-managed VPC or on-prem deployment; data does not leave customer network unless explicitly configured.

Q: How is data encrypted?
A: All traffic and data at rest are encrypted TLS 1.2+ and AES-256. For Private deployments, customers can integrate their KMS/HSM for root key management.

Q: Do you provide SOC2 / ISO / pen-test evidence?
A: Yes — we provide SOC2 Type II report summaries and third-party pen test summaries in the security pack under NDA.

Q: Can we use our identity provider and RBAC controls?
A: Yes — Redwood integrates with SAML/OAuth providers (Okta, Azure AD). Role-based access controls and audit logging are configurable per deployment.

Q: What isolation guarantees exist for Dedicated?
A: Dedicated uses reserved GPU pools with tenant-level isolation, network ACLs, and optional private peering. We also support encrypted KV caches scoped per-tenant.

Q: How do you handle model provenance and model updates?
A: Model catalog entries are versioned; rollouts support canary and A/B strategies, and we store provenance metadata for each model artifact and kernel config used in production.

Implementation & playbook (pilot -> production):
1) Technical discovery (week 0–1): collect sample prompts, expected qps, latency targets, dataset size, security constraints.
2) Pilot setup (week 1–3): provision Hosted or Dedicated test pool, run benchmark harness, collect latency/cost metrics.
3) Optimization (week 3–5): apply batching/cache/quantization recommendations, iterate prompts and model variant selection.
4) Security & compliance review (parallel): exchange security pack, configure KMS/VPC, run threat model.
5) Production rollout (week 6–10): canary traffic, SLO monitoring, full cutover and post-launch review.
